correctness.rationale: Exact Moore--Penrose reduction yields T=1/(p_i+p_j), probability (p_i+p_j)/4, and mean 5/2. For theta<2/5 the five-cycle excludes >=8 light pairs. Seven light pairs force either a heavy star (contradiction using light (1,5), (3,4) and mass order) or a heavy triangle; the cross-sum bound then yields W<=12theta-2, versus W<=6theta for <=6 edges. Constructed positive masses attain each envelope branch, including strict and equality boundary events. All steps are proved for arbitrary real positive normalized masses. Standard-library checker passed 127600 exact finite inequalities, 11 exact extremizers and 100 exact means; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The objective is the published rank-one pseudoinverse Frobenius stability measure under exact volume sampling. Its known expectation 5/2 does not provide thresholdwise input-uniform failure probabilities. The five-column two-sample case exhibits competing six- versus seven-edge extremizers, an exact risk-shape switch at t=3, and a 30-percentage-point right jump at the mean t=5/2, all quantitatively useful for small-budget volume-sampling reliability calibration. Structural graph classification and exact equality cases make this a substantive finite theorem rather than a mere unmotivated numerical slice; scope remains explicitly finite.
